source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: RBBB retains relatively normal initial depolarization with delayed terminal rightward forces, rsR-prime in V1/V2, broad lateral S waves and secondary ST-T changes.
Complete RBBB has QRS >= 120 ms; similar morphology with QRS < 120 ms is described as incomplete RBBB in the textbook.
LBBB changes initial depolarization direction, with absent lateral q waves, broad notched R waves, right-precordial QS/rS and secondary ST-T changes.
Bundle branch block alone does not require dropped AV conduction.

completeRight.morphology: Reuses the existing electrode tables and ST/T from right-bundle-block-illustration.json unchanged.

incompleteRight.morphology: Uses the complete RBBB normalized QRS table with support shortened to 110 ms. ST extends to T onset; QT and T remain unchanged. Amplitudes and 110 ms are authored choices, not measured textbook recordings.

completeLeft.morphology: Reuses the existing electrode tables and ST/T from left-bundle-block-illustration.json unchanged.

implementation: BundleBlockReference morphology options are independent of AvConductionPattern. The existing 4:3 Mobitz II combination and its samples are preserved.
limitations: Three fixed adult teaching examples, not bundle-conduction electrophysiology or anatomical models.
Incomplete RBBB directly reuses morphology and does not cover all terminal-force, ST/T or axis variants.
Incomplete LBBB, fascicular block, intermittent block and other rhythm combinations remain unimplemented.
No dyssynchrony, stroke-volume or automatic diagnostic inference. Existing mechanical-disable/perfusion settings remain independent.
Windows visual behavior is not yet manually verified.
